project.project_title: Paperback Cover: Blurb Edit & Font Consistency Fix

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hi Timothy
I have a quick job. Like to see if you’re free.

•	I have a paperback cover that needs 2 small fixes (delete a few words of my blurb + matching the title font across front/spine/back). No redesign, files are final otherwise. 
•	Output needed: .psd (layered), .pdf, .jpg 
•	Needed within 24 hours 
•	Are you available?

My budget is $30.

Best,
Caryn

value_updates.blurb_edit: delete a few words from the existing blurb

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hi Timothy, thanks for the speedy reply.

Two small fixes needed, not a redesign
Blurb swap: trimmed last paragraph, currently overlaps the barcode — just needs dropping in and reflowing
Title font inconsistent: front cover uses bold gold-gradient font, spine/back use a plainer one — need all matched to front
I'll send images, templates, and the .psd
Need .psd (layered), .pdf, .jpg back within 24 hours — does that work?

value_updates.layout_behavior: drop in and reflow the trimmed blurb so it does not overlap the barcode

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hi Timothy,

I'll post on D2D's social media. maybe that will get a faster response.

However, there's a problem with your cover.

• The blurb edit and title font look good, both fixed correctly.
• One problem: the tagline at the top of the front cover ("A CHINESE HOLIDAY MURDER MYSTERY") is showing as garbled, corrupted text instead of the actual words.
• This looks like a font substitution or encoding issue — please check what font that text box is using.
• When you re-export, make sure the fonts are embedded or outlined/converted to curves so the text doesn't depend on font availability and renders correctly everywhere.
• Please fix and re-send .pdf first

Thx
C-

execution.observed_behavior: The client reports that the blurb edit looks good and was fixed correctly.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: yes. It's 300 pages. FYI - I publish on Amazon (which the print book is 300 pages). But on Draft2Digital - they use Ingram (for print distribution) which added 2 pages to my book. I don't know if that affects the spine. So I am shortening my blurb since there's nothing I can do to stop D2D from making my page count 302 instead of 300. The issue is the bar code.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: You can see D2D's template has a spine of 0.68 inches but Amazon's is 0.75 inches.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: Of course. Right now I'm asking D2D if there's a bug. At 300–302 pages on Cream paper, the spine should be approximately 0.75", matching my Amazon file exactly — but D2D keeps generating 0.68", even after I followed their instructions to resave Step 2 and re-download the template fresh. I definitely want you do fix the blurb and font. Start on that. Will update you soon regard spine.

ambiguity.description: The required D2D spine width is unresolved because its template generates 0.68 inches while the client expects approximately 0.75 inches for the relevant page range.

source_message.text: I can't believe I still haven't heard from D2D. Let's hold off on this until tomorrow. I'll order something (which may or may not be the right specs for the cover). I will give them one more day. Thanks for your patience. Best, Caryn
